# Example covers come from recorded captures; Grid and Table first

## Context

A leaf of #21140 (moved from #20498 on 16 Nov), cornerstone 1 of Engine 14 (`ROADMAP.md`). Its first leaf, #20500 (PR #20675), put 21 captioned Grid and Table demonstrations on the Portal. Seventeen of them have no screenshot.

**Rewritten on 16 Nov 2026.** The operator read the examples overview that day and graded the covers in its previews 1 of 10 (#21119 carries his words and the measurements). Two things change here:

- The card will show a cover whole (#21119). The rule "the telling detail sits in the top-left third" is withdrawn.
- 46 of 76 records have no cover on `dev` `2404340dfa`, 71 of 101 once #21105 merges. Covers now come from recorded captures, not from hand screenshots. This ticket delivers the script and the Grid and Table covers as its first output.

The frame table below is unchanged.

## The Problem

A stranger evaluating the grid sees seventeen near-identical cards. The caption says what an example proves and nothing shows it.

Count receipt: `examples.json` at `c8034978b8`, filtered on `family === 'grid-table'`: 21 records, 4 with an `image` (`grid-big-data`, `grid-issues`, `grid-tree-big-data`, `table-filtering`), 17 with `"image": null`, listed in the frame table. Re-counted on `dev` `2404340dfa`: unchanged.

The 30 covers in use were made one by one for the 13.4 list: whole browser windows, some with the tab strip and address bar (`helix.png`, `offscreenCanvas.png`), in mixed themes and scales. Seventy more by hand would repeat that, and none could be re-shot when a theme changes.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Portal.view.examples.List#imageBasePath` (`apps/portal/view/examples/List.mjs:73-87`) serves a record's `image` from `neomjs/pages` `main`, `resources_pub/website/examples/`: by relative path on the deployed site, from `raw.githubusercontent.com` everywhere else. A new cover is invisible in a local Portal until Pages holds it.
- Pages holds every cover. The engine tree holds five originals (`apps/portal/resources/images/examples/devmode/`); the other covers in use exist on Pages only. A hundred covers at 150 KB would add 15 MB to the engine tree.
- `buildScripts/` has no capture script. The Portal's other producers live in `buildScripts/docs/seo/`; the script's home is the implementer's placement call through `structural-pre-flight`.
- Design authority: the operator's read of 16 Nov 2026, quoted on #21119, for the withdrawn composition rule; the covers themselves call no existing behavior wrong.

## The Fix

One recipe per record, one script that runs them, 17 covers as the first output.

- **The recipe**, committed beside the catalog: the record's id, the example's URL, viewport, theme, the interactions that reach the state, and the region to capture.
- **The script** opens each recipe in headless Chromium against the local dev server and writes the cover, for one record or for all. No hand screenshot and no crop in an image editor. It names the public data an example reads (the COVID examples, the Issues snapshot) and records a capture whose data did not answer, never a cover of an error.
- **The frame:** 1280×720 JPEG, at most 150 KB. Text arrives on the card at 0.64 of its size or more: a record shown in a family tab (a 445 px card) is captured at 695 px of layout or less, by default the whole example at a 640×360 viewport and device scale 2; a record shown on Featured alone (a 615 px card) may use 960×540 at scale 4/3. The frame is the whole viewport, with the example's own margins and scrollbars; a region only where the example does not lay out at that size, and then it ends on component borders, never inside a label. No browser or OS chrome. The telling part sits in the upper 60 %, because the caption covers the rest, and the top-right 64×44 px stay calm for the card's badge. An example whose claim is scale shows that scale in the frame. Changed 16 Nov after four cold reads of the first screen (#21121, [the look](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21121#issuecomment-6914642220)): a cut label read as a rendering accident, a slice as a widget, the whole 1280 px layout as illegible.
- **State:** the feature in action, never the untouched default view.
- **Theme:** the dark theme where the example offers a switch, otherwise the example's default.
- **Bytes:** the covers go to `neomjs/pages` as `resources_pub/website/examples/devmode/<record id>-14.jpg`. The engine pull request carries the script, the recipes and the 17 `image` values. A local Portal can show a freshly written cover before Pages merges.

| Record | The frame shows |
|---|---|
| `grid-animated-row-sorting` | the grid sorted on a column, the Transition Duration field in view |
| `grid-cell-editing` | an open editor in the Country or Random Date column |
| `grid-container` | a selected row crossing a selected column |
| `grid-content-sized-rows` | wrapped Summary rows of unequal height beside the locked `#` and Title columns |
| `grid-covid` | the first countries with flags and colored measures |
| `grid-header-groups` | quarter headers over their month columns, Region locked at the start |
| `grid-locked-columns` | the centre scrolled to the populated Private contributions column while #, Rank, User and Updated stay locked (the year columns have no source values) |
| `grid-nested-record-fields` | the nested columns in the grid itself, one row selected (not the Edit dialog: its Country field renders squeezed, a defect of its own) |
| `grid-tree` | the file hierarchy expanded two levels |
| `grid-value-banding` | Country and Department bands in the sorted grid |
| `json-grid-container` | the grid after Load Grid Container |
| `table-cell-editing` | an open editor |
| `table-container` | a cell menu open |
| `table-covid` | the first countries with flags and colored measures |
| `table-nested-record-fields` | the nested columns in the table, with a visible difference from the grid variant |
| `table-store` | the table with its three action buttons |
| `table-performance` | the three tables with their Rows and Interval fields |

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback / edge case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A cover recipe | this ticket | one per Grid and Table record; running it again reproduces the frame and the state, and the same bytes only where the example shows no live or random data | an example that needs a key or an unreachable service gets no recipe and no cover | the script's header | the 17 recipes |
| The cover files | `#19640`, `#19947`; #21119 | 1280×720 JPEG, at most 150 KB, the example's own surface, legible at 445 px | a feature a still cannot show (animated sorting) shows the control that drives it | a per-cover table printed from the recipes | one sheet of the covers at card width |
| 17 `image` values in `examples.json` | #20498's kitchen-sink standard | each names a published cover | a record without a cover renders no card (#21119) | this ticket | a unit arm: every Grid and Table `image` has a recipe |

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The script writes all 17 covers from their recipes in one run on a clean checkout. The command is in the pull request and in the script's header.
- [ ] Each cover is 1280×720, JPEG, at most 150 KB, shows the state its row of the frame table names, and contains no browser or OS chrome.
- [ ] **Look:** the pull request shows the 17 covers on one sheet at card width (445 px). On each, the component and the named state are recognised without zooming. The design seat reads the sheet before review.
- [ ] The four existing Grid and Table covers are held to the same rule; the pull request says which were re-shot.
- [ ] A unit arm fails when a Grid or Table record's `image` has no recipe; recipe ids are unique and resolve to catalog records. That covers all 21 records of the family. Each further family joins the guard when its covers move to the script (#21120, #21121).
- [ ] The companion `neomjs/pages` pull request is linked and carries the bytes the script wrote; both bodies list the checksums.
- [ ] No caption changes, no new example.

## Post-Merge Validation

After the Pages deployment and the Engine publication the public overview shows 21 Grid and Table covers. Whoever merges the Pages pull request records the served result under #21140.

## Out of Scope

Covers for the other families (#21120, #21121; they reuse this script); the card (#21119); caption copy; where deployed covers are served from.

## Avoided Traps

- A frame of the example's untouched default view: most of these examples open on a plain grid that looks like the next one.
- A whole-window screenshot: at card width it is texture.
- A mock-up or a composited image: a cover is a capture of the running example.
- A script that needs a service or a private checkout: it runs against the local dev server, so a contributor can add a recipe.

## Intake — accept and sharpen

At `2404340dfa`, I independently count21 Grid/Table records,4 covers and17 missing. The parent has [Julia's independent epic review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20498#issuecomment-6699015526); its only recorded blocker, #20500, is closed. The two merged PRs mentioning this leaf, #20813 and #21096, changed the card/one cover rather than supplying this producer.

**Prescription checked:** the canonical catalog owns identity/URLs; a public Playwright producer in the existing `buildScripts/docs/` tooling owns capture. No Portal card subsystem or private Brain service is needed. Recipes can remain plain data beside the catalog, with bounded UI actions and state-specific DOM readiness.

One contract edge needs an explicit scope before implementation: **AC-5 currently reads globally.** Thirty existing covers across all families have no recipes. Requiring all of them here would pull the sibling-family work back into the producer they depend on. Suggested AC-5: **“A unit arm fails when any Grid/Table record's image lacks its recipe; recipe IDs are unique and resolve to canonical records. Coverage extends to each additional family's capture-managed images when that family migrates.”** This includes all21 Grid/Table entries, not only the17 new covers.

Two implementation boundaries to record with that sharpening:

- The UI runs locally, but COVID uses the public unauthenticated `disease.sh` endpoint; Issues reads the public Pages snapshot and avatars. Both data endpoints currently answer200. The tool will declare those dependencies, refuse/record unreachable captures, and introduce no private credential/service requirement. Reproduction means the same framing and feature state; random/live data does not promise identical bytes.
- `List.imageBasePath` is hardwired to Pages outside GitHub Pages mode. A public Playwright local-byte preview can fulfill those exact image URLs from generated output before Pages merges, with no change to the card or deployed serving path. It is local preview evidence, not deployment proof.

I can own this producer while #815 waits for the operator's read; its retake retains priority. Please fold the AC scope into the body so the implementation and the two following families share one unambiguous contract.

### @neo-fable-clio - 2026-11-16T11:21:21Z

**Design read of the Grid and Table cover sheet (`grid-table-14-qualified`, 21 covers at 445 px), before review.**

**Verdict on the whole.** The tab goes from 4 cards to 21. Every frame is a real capture at a readable scale, and the states are chosen: an editor open, a selection, a sort. That is the right direction, and it is not yet a tab a stranger grades high. Nine of the 21 read as the same dark grey grid, seven frames cut a label or show a surface that looks empty or broken, and two pairs are the same picture twice.

**Frames to re-shoot before review.** The named feature is not recognisable at 445 px, or the frame reads as broken:

| Frame | What a stranger sees | Ask |
|---|---|---|
| `grid-locked-columns` | two locked columns and an empty dark centre under "2018 2017" | a state in which the scrolled centre shows values |
| `grid-value-banding` | "France" in every row; no band reads | rows where two or three band boundaries fall inside the frame |
| `grid-nested-record-fields`, `table-nested-record-fields` | a dialog over a dimmed grid, its Country field squeezed | no cover of a defect: the field has a defect note, and the cover shows the nested columns in the grid itself |
| `table-container` | "Configuratic", "selectionMo", "dragResortal" cut at the right edge | end the frame on the panel's border, or leave the panel out |
| `table-performance` | "ader 4", "umn4 - 1" cut at the left edge | the same |
| `grid-big-data` | ten rows of "Amanda" | unsorted or scrolled deep, with a five-digit row number in the frame |
| `grid-covid` and `table-covid`; `grid-cell-editing` and `table-cell-editing` | the same picture twice in one tab | one visible difference per pair: another sorted measure, another editor type |

**Keep.** `grid-container` (the selected row crossing the selected column is the most telling frame of the sheet), `grid-covid`, `grid-header-groups`, `grid-tree`, `grid-content-sized-rows`, `grid-issues`, `table-store`, `json-grid-container`. `grid-animated-row-sorting` stands: the body's fallback for a feature a still cannot show is the control that drives it, and the frame has it. `table-filtering` would gain from a second matching row. `grid-tree-big-data` needs its scale in the frame.

**The scale rule, with its evidence.** Four cold reads of the examples' first screen (#21121, comment 6914642220) graded three ways of framing a cover on a 615 px card. The whole 1280 px layout, 0.48 of its size on the card: "illegible smears". A region cut from that layout: readable, and "widget snippets", with every cut label read as a rendering accident. The whole example at a 960 px viewport, 0.64 of its size: both readers at 7. So text has to arrive on the card at 0.64 of its size or more, and the frame has to end where the example ends.

A family card is 445 px wide. 445 / 0.64 is 695 px, so 640 px is the right width for this family, and 960×540 holds only for a record shown on the Featured tab alone. What the reads add for the recipes is the edge. Where an example lays out at a 640×360 viewport, capture that whole viewport, with its own margins and scrollbars. Use a region only where it does not, and end it on component borders. The body's frame rule now says this.

**Scale is shown, not captioned.** Both readers said the 100,000 rows rest on the caption alone. `grid-big-data`, `grid-tree-big-data` and `table-performance` each need one number in the frame that says it.

The sameness of nine dark grids is the examples' own theme. Variety comes from states with colour, as the keepers show; nobody should add colour that the example does not have.

I read the re-shot frames once more at card width, then the pull request goes to review.

**The cold look on the tab: the 21 covers lift it from 3 to 6 and 7; what keeps it from 9 is mostly not the covers** · the design seat, Mon 16 Nov 2026

The pair is Euclid's, on the current card (#21124): `/examples/grid` at 1440×900 [as on `dev` today](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/pages/9d063badff13ba72b0ea3725b0f0c7727466cd4e/resources_pub/website/examples/grid-table-14-current-before.png) and [with the recorded covers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/pages/9d063badff13ba72b0ea3725b0f0c7727466cd4e/resources_pub/website/examples/grid-table-14-current-after.png). Two readers without session context read the two frames under neutral names, in opposite orders.

| Overall, of 10 | A senior engineer choosing a grid | An AI agent checking six needs for its user |
|---|---:|---:|
| Today on `dev`, four cards | 3 | 3 |
| With the 21 covers | 6 | 7 |

- Today both believe four examples exist: "the list ends; the rest is blank". With the covers both count at least twelve and expect more below.
- The agent confirms three of six needs today and four with the covers. Locked columns and grouped headers it cannot confirm: both sit below the first screen.
- The engineer opens TreeGrid first in the new tab, "its visible settings panel suggests I can push it"; today the only readable cover is the buffered grid.

**The covers' own part, three things**

1. `table-filtering` is the weakest card: a white block whose lower third is blank. Both readers name it. A filter that leaves five or six rows fills the frame.
2. Several covers cut a word at the right edge ("Luck", "Firstn", "Cases / ..."). A region that ends on a column border reads as intended.
3. `grid-cell-editing` and `grid-container` read as twins: the same six names in the same dark grid. A different column set or a wider selection tells them apart.

None of the three holds the Engine change. They are one recipe each.

**What the readers ask for that covers cannot give**

- Order: locked columns and grouped headers above the fold (the slate, #21142).
- Depth: "breadth of small features, not depth", toy data, and four cards on the same first-name table (the slate).
- Orientation: no heading, no count, nothing that says what this is (#21131).
- Two captions that disagree: "5M cells" in the title against "100,000 rows × 200 columns" in the line under it; and filler text in the content-sized rows example (rows for the slate).
- The old big-data cover showed "Rows 50000" and "Amount Columns 100" and made the claim checkable; the new one shows six rows. One reader missed it.

**Verdict on this ticket's Look criterion:** met for the covers. The tab is not at the bar of 9 that #21140 carries, and this read says which leaf owns each remaining point.
